chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who performed one circuit or two circuits of Tawaaf, then went out with a man for a need, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If it was an optional Tawaaf, he builds upon it (completes the circuits), and if it was an obligatory Tawaaf, he does not build upon it (i.e., repeats it).'

key_terms.بَنَى عَلَيْهِ: Builds upon it (continues from where left off)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on completing Tawaaf if one is interrupted by a need?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between Nafilah and Fard Tawaaf when interrupted by necessity, establishing that optional circuits are cumulative while obligatory ones are nullified. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the strict conditions of validity for pillar acts, contrasting with some Sunni schools that may view interruption as merely breaking the continuity rather than invalidating the act entirely. It underscores the principle that the intention and type of worship dictate the rigor of its completion requirements.
